questions.q: What does a Campaign object represent?
options: A specific, tracked marketing initiative, such as an email blast, webinar, or trade show
A single deal in progress
An individual person's contact record
A customer support issue
questions.explain: A Campaign is a named, tracked marketing effort with its own dates, budget fields, and targeted audience.

questions.q: How is a Campaign different from the Lead Source field?
options: A Campaign is a specific, trackable initiative with its own record; Lead Source is just a single, broad field on a Lead
They are exactly the same thing with two different names
Lead Source is more granular than a Campaign
A Campaign can only ever be linked to one single Lead
questions.explain: Campaign is a full, detailed record of a marketing effort, far more granular than the broad category captured in Lead Source.

options: The join record connecting a Campaign to a specific Lead or Contact, tracking their status
A Salesforce user with admin permissions over Campaigns
A synonym for Opportunity
A field on the Account object
questions.explain: Campaign Member links a Campaign to a Lead or Contact and records status values like Sent, Responded, or Attended.

questions.q: What field on the Opportunity object records which Campaign gets primary credit for the deal?
options: Primary Campaign Source
Lead Source
Stage
Rating
questions.explain: Primary Campaign Source is the field on Opportunity that most Campaign ROI reports rely on.

questions.q: What is the real relationship path from a Campaign to the revenue it influenced?
options: Campaign to Campaign Member to Lead/Contact to Opportunity
Campaign directly to Case, with no other objects involved
There is no traceable relationship between Campaigns and revenue
Campaign to Account, skipping Leads and Contacts entirely
questions.explain: Campaign Members link a Campaign to Leads/Contacts, which convert into Opportunities — making the ROI path traceable end to end.
